===== SUMMARY.md =====
# F35 — the `@ll` boundary is the envelope's link-header length, and it is 0 inside an L3 tunnel

**Turn 557.** Owner's words: *«Проверь ll на VLAN/туннелях»*. Generated by
`tools/f35_summary.py` from `logs/f35_*.log`; `tools/audit_f35_doc.py` re-runs
the generator and refuses to let this file drift from the logs.

The guard under test is `nft_ll_write_ok()` in 7.3.4:

```c
static bool nft_ll_write_ok(const struct nft_pktinfo *pkt, int offset)
{
        if (nft_in_ingress(pkt->state)) return true;
        return offset <= skb_network_offset(pkt->skb);
}
```

called with `offset = priv->len + priv->offset + (skb_mac_header - skb->data) - vlan_hlen`,
while `skb_network_offset()` in 7.3 is `skb_network_header() - skb->data`. Substituting,
the condition is

```
priv->offset + priv->len  <=  skb_network_header - skb_mac_header + vlan_hlen
```

i.e. **the write must end inside this envelope's link header.** On ethernet that
number is 14, which is what F33 measured. This finding asks what it is when the
envelope is not a bare ethernet frame.

## 1. One grid, seven envelopes, one boot

36-cell `(offset,len)` grid (`offset ∈ {0,1,2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,20,24}`, `len ∈ {1,2,4}`), the tunnel envelopes on a 21-cell grid (`offset ∈ {0,6,10,12,14,16,20}`). Oracle per cell: the kernel's own counter,
placed **after** the store in the same rule — `cnt=1` means the guard passed the
store and the rest of the rule ran, `cnt=0` means the store was refused.

| envelope | alive / cells | control (no store) |
|---|---|---|
| ip, plain, **F33's own helper** (2 s ACK window) | **23/36** | — |
| ip, plain, fast helper | **23/36** | 1 |
| ip, 802.1Q frame | **0/36** | 0 |
| bridge, plain | **23/36** | 1 |
| bridge, 802.1Q frame | **25/36** | 1 |
| **ipip** L3 tunnel, inner packet | **0/21** | 1 |
| **vxlan** L2 tunnel, inner packet | **11/21** | 1 |

Three things this table already says without any theory:

* plain ethernet in the **ip** family and in the **bridge** family give the same
  accept-set, cell for cell — the family is not the variable;
* the **ipip** envelope has **no** live cell at all, not even `(0,1)`;
* the **vxlan** envelope gives exactly the plain-ethernet set: 11/21.

## 2. The cells that move when the frame is tagged

Same datagram, same hook (bridge prerouting), same grid — the only difference is
four bytes of 802.1Q between the MAC addresses and the ethertype:

| cell | plain (cnt) | 802.1Q (cnt) | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| (10,4) | 1 | 0 | straddles the tag: `nft_payload_need_vlan_adjust()` sends it into `nft_payload_set_vlan()`, which only knows offsets 12 and 14 |
| (12,1) | 1 | 0 | offset 12 with `len=1` is neither `h_vlan_proto` (len 2/4) nor `h_vlan_TCI` (len 2): the vlan branch refuses it, the plain branch allowed it |
| (12,4) | 0 | 1 | offset 12 with `len=4` inserts the whole tag into skb metadata (`__vlan_hwaccel_put_tag`) — the plain branch had no such door |
| (14,2) | 0 | 1 | `h_vlan_TCI`: writes `skb->vlan_tci`, the tag never appears in the frame |
| (16,1) | 0 | 1 | **the ethertype byte**: `vlan_hlen=4` is subtracted from the base, so the limit is **18**, not 14 |
| (16,2) | 0 | 1 | **the ethertype**: same branch, full 16-bit store |

`(16,4)` stays dead on both (16+4 = 20 > 18) and every `offset ≥ 20` cell stays
dead on both — the new branch has its own limit, it is not open-ended.

## 3. Under `policy drop` the same rule accepts untagged traffic and drops tagged traffic

Chain policy `drop`, one rule per arm, ending in `counter accept`; the control arm
has the same chain and no store.

| arm | frame | control | cnt |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | plain | 1 | — |
| `b12_1` | plain | — | **1** |
| `b14_2` | plain | — | **0** |
| `b16_2` | plain | — | **0** |
| — | 802.1Q | 1 | — |
| `b12_1` | 802.1Q | — | **0** |
| `b14_2` | 802.1Q | — | **1** |
| `b16_2` | 802.1Q | — | **1** |

Read the two blocks together: `@ll,96,8` (offset 12, len 1) **delivers** an
untagged frame and **discards** a tagged one; `@ll,128,16` (offset 16, len 2)
does the exact opposite. The controls are 1, so neither column is "the frame
never arrived".

## 4. The same grid inside real tunnels

No image this project had booted could decapsulate anything (`CONFIG_NET_IPIP`
and `CONFIG_VXLAN` were unset), so T557 = T556 + those two symbols; `nft_payload.c`,
`nft_cmp.c`, `nft_meta.c`, `ipip.c`, `vxlan_core.c` are **byte-identical** to the
parent (checked). The outer datagram is sent with `IP_HDRINCL` and the kernel's own
routing; the chain is gated on `meta iif == <tunnel device>`, so the outer packet
is not counted. Control arm (no store, same gate): **1** for ipip, **1** for vxlan.

| envelope | live cells of 21 | identical to |
|---|---|---|
| ipip (L3) | **0** | — |
| vxlan (L2) | **11** | plain ethernet, cell for cell |

Why: `ipip_tunnel_rcv()` calls `skb_reset_mac_header()` right after pulling the
outer header, so `mac_header == data` and the limit is **0** — every `@ll` store
dies, including offset 0. `vxlan_set_mac()` calls `skb_reset_mac_header()` and
then `eth_type_trans()`, so the inner frame is an ordinary ethernet frame and the
limit is 14 again. The envelope, not the write, decides.

## 5. What is NOT measured, and one thing that is measured as a limit

**802.1Q in the ip family is not measured in this build.** T557 has
`# CONFIG_VLAN_8021Q is not set`: the receive path never untags the frame, so the
IPv4 stack never sees it. Three independent probes in one boot:

| probe | value |
|---|---|
| ip prerouting counter, plain frame | 1
 |
| ip prerouting counter, 802.1Q frame | **0
** |
| netdev **ingress** counter, same 802.1Q frame | 1
 |
| `IpInReceives` before / after the plain frame | ? → ? |
| `IpInReceives` after the 802.1Q frame | ? (unchanged) |

So the tagged frame reaches the device driver and the ingress hook and then
disappears before IPv4 — a config fact, not a guard behaviour. With
`CONFIG_VLAN_8021Q=y` the ip-family arms would be measurable, and the prediction
for them is the same set the bridge envelope produced (§2): the arithmetic is
envelope-local and does not mention the family.

Also not measured, stated plainly: the **bytes** an accepted `(16,2)` store leaves
on the wire. NFLOG at the bridge hook logs from the network header (every hex
starts `4500…`), and the AF_PACKET capture on the bridge's far side only ever
returned ICMPv6 noise — the capture instrument for that sentence does not exist
yet, so the target byte is a reading of `skb_reorder_vlan_header()` + the
`vlan_hlen` subtraction, not a measurement. Also untouched: IPv6 and ARP inside
both tunnels, GSO/`CHECKSUM_PARTIAL`, QinQ, `@ih` on a tagged inner frame, and
the same grid at the netdev **egress** hook with a tag in metadata.

## 6. What this changes

F33 called the `ll` branch a *boundary*, and a boundary sounds like a constant.
It is not: it is the length of the current envelope's link header. Two consequences
worth a line in the letter:

1. **A rule that works on ethernet is silently dead on tunneled traffic.**
   `@ll,0,48 set …` (rewrite the destination MAC) installs everywhere and does
   nothing to a packet that came out of an ipip device; under `policy drop` the
   rule then discards every packet arriving from that tunnel.
2. **A tagged frame has two boundaries in one expression** — 14 for stores that
   stay below the tag, 18 for stores that touch the ethertype area — and the
   second one accepts a store (`offset 16`) that the untagged envelope refuses.

## 7. Mistakes of this turn, all mine

1. **`meta iif` compared in the wrong byte order.** `nft_meta_store_ifindex()`
   writes `*dest = ifindex` (native), `nft_cmp` compares raw bytes, and I
   compared against `htonl()`: every gated arm was 0, *including* a gate on the
   device the frame demonstrably arrives on. Found by a control, not by reading.
2. **`ip link add t557 type ipip` → -EEXIST.** `ipip_init_net()` already creates
   the fallback `tunl0` with all-zero params, so a second zero-param tunnel is a
   duplicate. Measured (`ipip_bare=-17`, `ipip_second_name=-17`), then `tunl0`
   was used instead.
3. **`IFLA_VXLAN_ID` is native u32, not big-endian** (`nla_get_u32`): with
   `htonl(557)` the kernel read 754974720 and answered -ERANGE.
4. **A hand-built outer ipip frame never reaches the tunnel.** It passes ip
   prerouting and then disappears without a single IP counter moving
   (`IpInReceives` +1, `InDelivers`/`ForwDatagrams`/`InAddrErrors` +0). Sending
   the same outer header with `IP_HDRINCL` and the kernel's own routing
   decapsulates (`tunl0` rx +2 for 2 sends), so the raw socket is what the arms
   use; the cause of the hand-built drop is **not** isolated.
5. **`cap_open()` sets `O_NONBLOCK`** and veth delivers through NAPI, so the
   capture returned EAGAIN immediately. Fixed with a poll loop — and then the
   first frame captured was ICMPv6 noise, which is why §5 says the byte
   evidence is missing rather than wrong.
6. **The F33 helper's NFLOG socket is `NFL33`**, opened by `f556_main()`, which
   this instrument never calls: the `p4s` reference envelope therefore has
   `nfl=0` on live cells. The verifier excludes it from the log check and says
   so.
7. **CRLF, eighth time in this project**: every `$`-anchored regex in the new
   verifier matched zero rows until it became `\r?$`.
8. Parser field counts: the first version of the F33-regression regex expected
   five fields before `cnt` where the line has four.

## 8. How it is checked

| instrument | result |
|---|---|
| `tools/verify557.py` | **110 checks, 0 fail** — kernel hash against the hash its own log recorded, differ extracted from the initramfs and compared with `vm/build/differ557` (`2f1f9c0530727d48`), config delta = exactly the three tunnel symbols, five source files byte-identical to T556, every grid cell against a Python model of the guard, controls, the six-cell VLAN difference, the two tunnel identities, the verdict block, the config limit, two full boots + three cross-boot comparisons, the F33 regression, 0 splat |
| `tools/verify557_selftest.sh` | **14/14 mutations red**, baseline green |
| `tools/audit_f35_doc.py` | regenerates this file and diffs it |
| regression | `verify556` 1847, `verify555` 140, `verify553` 311, `verify552` 5633, `verify551` 1802, `verify_f2` 193 |

Kernel: `src/linux-7.3.4-T557`, bzImage `e263d55750c47c72b6df3b6cf1db4192`, initrd `396d31a2b57a19cb`.
Counted boots: `f35_T_rep1`, `f35_T_rep2` (208 arms each), `f35_T_grid` (148),
`f35_T_ver` (14), `f35_T_tun` (44); 8 diagnostic boots (`f557diag`..`f557diag11`,
`bytes`) that found the four instrument faults in §7 and are not counted as
measurements of the guard.

Arms in the counted boots were run twice: `T_rep1` vs `T_rep2` (same 208 arms,
same counters) and, across boots, `T_grid` and `T_tun` against `T_rep1`.
